- When sentiment is negative in the recent history, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peaks at 1–2% below true high.
- If sentiment is consistently positive, model tends to overestimate future prices; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 3-day horizon.
- Model underestimates true price when recent sentiment is mixed (e.g., 0.00 values) — adjust upward by 0.5–1.0% for the next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% gap), assume mean reversion bias — apply upward correction proportional to sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price by 2–4 days — adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day sentiment momentum shift.
- When sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underestimate — apply +0.5% to +1.5% correction for next 5 days.
